business: SunXFinder: a free website and Android app in Sudan to size a home solar system and compare written offers from several local solar companies
target: Adults in Khartoum and Port Sudan who are planning to buy a home or shop solar system in the next 6 months, including Sudanese abroad paying for a family system
where: Khartoum and Port Sudan, Sudan (plus Sudanese abroad in Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar and Egypt)

segments.name: Homeowner in Khartoum or Port Sudan running a generator or living with long power cuts
Small shop owner (grocery, pharmacy, phone shop, tailor) losing sales in power cuts
Sudanese working abroad paying for a solar system for family in Sudan

behaviours.name: Asks family and friends first
behaviours.how: Uses the installer a relative or neighbour used, and trusts word of mouth over any website.

behaviours.name: Facebook group asker
behaviours.how: Posts 'who installed yours and how much?' in a city or solar Facebook group and reads the comments.

behaviours.name: Market haggler
behaviours.how: Goes to the market, compares parts prices shop by shop, and has a local electrician wire it.

behaviours.name: Careful researcher
behaviours.how: Reads about panels, batteries and inverters, wants brands and models in writing before paying.

behaviours.name: Already has an installer
behaviours.how: Has spoken to one company already and is close to deciding.

behaviours.name: Budget stretcher
behaviours.how: Wants to start small with what they can afford now and add more later; price decides everything.

objections: I don't know what size system I need, so I can't judge any offer
Panels and batteries in the market are often fake or weak; how would an app know?
I'd rather use the installer my relative used than a stranger from an app
I'm worried companies will call me non-stop once they have my number
Prices change with the dollar every week; a quote today is useless next week
Is this app even working? I don't want to download something empty
Solar is simply too expensive for me right now
From abroad I can't check that the company actually did the work
habits: the power is cut for about 12 hours a day in your area
you spend a lot on generator fuel every month and it is not always available
you use WhatsApp all day and Facebook every evening
your phone is an Android with limited storage and mobile data
a neighbour installed solar last year and you heard mixed things about it
you send money home every month through a relative or a transfer app
